governanceNotes: Hydronephrosis edge authored at DIRECT_CAUSATION with PROBABLE consensus and hypothesizedOnly:false, following the urethral-stricture precedent: detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia/underactive-bladder outflow obstruction and high-pressure storage mechanically overwhelm the ureterovesical junction, producing vesicoureteral reflux and upper-tract dilatation; the claim is scoped to documented dysfunctional voiding with clinically significant upper-tract change, not to any cystitis diagnosis.

Stones edge held at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the StatPearls etiology language and SCI excess-risk review document the stasis pathway qualitatively, but no cohort quantifies incident stone formation in non-SCI neurogenic-bladder populations, and catheter use confounds attribution (catheter encrustation and infection are independent stone drivers).

Treatment-interruption guard recorded in-file: CIC, antimuscarinics, botulinum toxin, and surgical management each interrupt the stasis/high-pressure pathway; chronology and persistence under documented management must be shown.

nexusClaim.etiologicalTrigger: Documented neurogenic bladder dysfunction (detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia or detrusor underactivity) -> clinically significant high-pressure storage/voiding or incomplete emptying -> overwhelmed ureterovesical junction with vesicoureteral reflux or direct back-pressure -> claimed hydronephrosis.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: An outflow-obstruction/back-pressure pathway: neurogenic detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia or an underactive bladder produces high-pressure storage against a closed sphincter or chronic residual urine; when the normal ureterovesical junction is overwhelmed, urine refluxes to the upper tract and sustained back-pressure dilates the renal pelvis - the same mechanical dilatation pathway the knowledge base records for urethral stricture. Treatment (catheterization, antimuscarinics, botulinum toxin, augmentation) interrupts the pathway, so documented chronology under management is required.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The mechanism is the established urodynamic consequence of dysfunctional voiding and is the same obstruction-mechanical pathway already modeled as DIRECT_CAUSATION for urethral stricture -> hydronephrosis; the claim is scoped to documented neurogenic dysfunction with imaging-confirmed upper-tract dilatation. Etiological consensus is PROBABLE for the scoped mechanical claim.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: urodynamic or documented neurogenic-bladder diagnosis (detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia, neurogenic detrusor underactivity, or comparable high-pressure/retention phenotype); renal-bladder ultrasound or CT documenting hydronephrosis with laterality and grade; chronology linking the bladder diagnosis to the dilatation; exclusion of independent upper-tract obstruction (stones, stricture, tumor); documentation of bladder-management status at the time dilatation was found
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Urolithiasis at the ureterovesical junction or ureter
Urethral stricture or other anatomical obstruction

suggestions.rationale: Authored at DIRECT_CAUSATION following the urethral-stricture precedent, with the mechanical pathway scoped to clinically significant dilatation and independent obstruction excluded; hypothesizedOnly is false because the pathway is the established urodynamic consequence, not a speculation.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The StatPearls bladder-stone review states adult bladder stone formation is most often associated with urinary stasis from bladder outlet obstruction or neurogenic bladder dysfunction (Leslie 2026); the SCI-focused literature review documents excess kidney and bladder stone risk in neurogenic bladder populations (Ruffion 2007); the neurogenic-bladder UTI review lists urinary stasis, high bladder pressure, and bladder stones among the population's risk factors, documenting the reciprocal stasis-stone-infection interaction (Dinh 2019).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the quantified excess-risk data are spinal-cord-injury cohorts rather than all-cause neurogenic bladder, catheter use independently drives encrustation and infection stones, immobilization and metabolic factors contribute in SCI, and no incidence denominator exists for non-SCI neurogenic bladder populations.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A urinary-stasis pathway is hypothesized: incomplete emptying and high residual volumes allow crystal nucleation and stone growth in the bladder, while stasis plus recurrent infection raises upper-tract stone risk; the pathway is anatomically and chemically standard but its magnitude in non-SCI neurogenic bladder is unquantified, and intermittent catheterization both mitigates and (via catheter-related infection) complicates it.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Stasis-mediated stone formation is the standard teaching and the SCI excess risk is documented, but population-specific incidence, catheter confounding, and treatment interruption keep this below causal strength. Etiological consensus is therefore NOT_ESTABLISHED and the mapping asserts no nexus probability.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: stone documentation by imaging or passage with composition analysis where available; neurogenic-bladder diagnosis with urodynamic phenotype and chronology; residual-volume/voiding documentation showing stasis; catheter-use history (indwelling vs intermittent, encrustation history); metabolic stone workup (24-hour urine or serum studies)
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Chronic UTI with urease-producing organisms independent of stasis

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the stasis pathway is standard but the quantified evidence is SCI-specific and catheter use confounds attribution; no causal or aggravation claim is made.
